claims.title: Pair admissibility local factor
claims.statement: For a nonzero gap g modulo q, the two forbidden start residues are 0 and -g, so the standard local obstruction count for H={0,g} is nu_q(H)=2 and the admissible-start count is q-2.
claims.scope: Finite residue arithmetic over ZMod q with [NeZero q] and g nonzero modulo q; this is the k=2 Hardy-Littlewood local factor, not a global prime-distribution theorem.

provenance.prior_art: Classical Hardy-Littlewood singular-series local obstruction factor nu_q(H).
provenance.artifact_status: Lean source reports AXLE verification; source-byte, pinned local-build, and saved axiom-report evidence remain to be consolidated before V4/V5 promotion.
provenance.notes: The contribution claimed here is formalization and reusable local-sieve infrastructure, not novelty in analytic number theory.

claims.falsifier_or_failure_mode: A counterexample to the finite cardinality identity, a source/signature mismatch, or a failed rebuild invalidates this record.
claims.public_wording: Machine-checked formalization of the standard pair-admissibility local factor; no new prime-distribution result is claimed.

claims.title: Goldbach local count and centered spike
claims.statement: For prime p, the number of ordered pairs of nonzero residues summing to c is p-1 when c=0 and p-2 otherwise; the centered form is the finite spike 1_{c=0}-1/p.
claims.scope: Finite arithmetic in ZMod p. It does not transfer a local covariance kernel to a global Goldbach correlation.

provenance.artifact_status: Source is present in the verified-core repository; release-grade V4/V5 evidence is not asserted by this record.
provenance.notes: The global Goldbach-transfer interpretation remains outside this exact finite theorem.

claims.falsifier_or_failure_mode: A failed finite-field count, mismatched theorem statement, or unsatisfied proof gate invalidates the claim.
claims.public_wording: Exact finite local count formalized in Lean; no global Goldbach consequence is claimed.

claims.title: Cycle-spectrum rigidity of the golden value
claims.statement: For prime p, the occurrence of phi-1=2 cos(2 pi / 5) in the stated cycle-spectrum model forces p=5. The current Lean proof uses the exact cosine relation; the paper must also state the short conductor-5 cyclotomic explanation.
claims.scope: Cycle-spectrum rigidity. It does not imply a special global law for prime distribution modulo 5.

provenance.prior_art: Elementary cosine/cyclotomic rigidity; for exposition, Q(sqrt(5)) has conductor 5.
provenance.artifact_status: Lean source records an AXLE verification header; the current V5 manifest must still provide source-byte, local-build, and saved-axiom evidence before final verification language is used.
provenance.notes: The scientific value is a machine-checked cycle-spectrum rigidity statement, not numerological privilege for five.

claims.falsifier_or_failure_mode: A mismatch between the formal spectrum definition and the stated cyclotomic implication, or failure of the verified proof artifact, invalidates the claim.
claims.public_wording: Machine-checked rigidity for a cycle-spectrum value; no prime-distribution consequence is claimed.

claims.title: Fixed-modulus prime-pairs-in-AP hypothesis
claims.statement: For fixed q and gap g, real prime-pair counts in each admissible residue class admit a named Hardy-Littlewood-style main term with lower-order error.
claims.scope: Fixed modulus q only. This record deliberately makes no uniformity-in-q claim.

hypotheses_carried.name: Brockian.Hypothesis.PrimePairsInAPAtModulus
hypotheses_carried.range: A single fixed modulus q and fixed gap g.
hypotheses_carried.description: A conjectural asymptotic tied to the actual prime-pair count; it is neither established by Bombieri-Vinogradov nor supplied as a Lean instance.

provenance.prior_art: Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair conjectural framework refined to a fixed arithmetic progression.
provenance.artifact_status: New interface specification; no proof instance exists.
provenance.notes: Conditional theorems must carry this proposition as an explicit argument.

claims.falsifier_or_failure_mode: A counterexample to the stated asymptotic or any attempt to provide an implicit/global instance without evidence invalidates the use of this hypothesis.
claims.public_wording: Open hypothesis for a fixed modulus; it is not a theorem and does not prove equidistribution.

claims.title: Uniform prime-pairs-in-AP hypothesis
claims.statement: For a fixed gap g and an explicitly supplied modulus range Q(X), the per-class prime-pair asymptotic holds with an error term uniform for q less than or equal to Q(X).
claims.scope: The strength is determined by the supplied range Q; examples such as logarithmic ranges and power ranges must be named in every downstream theorem.

hypotheses_carried.name: Brockian.Hypothesis.UniformPrimePairsInAP
hypotheses_carried.range: Exactly q <= Q(X), where Q is an explicit argument; no unnamed level of distribution is permitted.
hypotheses_carried.description: A conjectural uniform prime-pair asymptotic. It is not implied by Bombieri-Vinogradov. For Q(X) tending to infinity, it is stronger than a fixed-modulus formulation.

provenance.prior_art: Uniform Hardy-Littlewood-type prime-pair asymptotics in arithmetic progressions.
provenance.artifact_status: New interface specification; no proof instance exists.
provenance.notes: This is the only hypothesis name to use for results that consume a q-range.

claims.falsifier_or_failure_mode: Failure in the named range, ambiguity about Q, or use of a fixed-q result as though it were uniform invalidates the claim.
claims.public_wording: Open uniformity hypothesis with an explicit modulus range; it is not implied by Bombieri-Vinogradov.
